verdict.rationale: Gmail's API documents OAuth 2.0 scopes and tells developers to pick the narrowest one, including non-sensitive and read-only scopes. OAuth also covers IMAP/SMTP access, so an agent can be given a least-privilege grant. However, the credential is an OAuth app grant set up through a developer flow, not a user-issued agent token, and community reports note scopes can't be limited to a specific label and that Google restricts third-party OAuth apps. Missing for 10: a user-facing way to mint agent-specific credentials, label- or folder-level scoping, documented revocation and audit of agent grants, and hands-on corroboration of the issuance flow.
